notes: Structure assertions (Given/When/Then scenarios, Missing-tests list, red-before-green instruction, done-when tied to tests) went 100% with skill vs 0% without across all three evals — this is where the skill does its work. Baselines wrote competent traditional reports (Expected behavior prose, acceptance checkboxes) but never test-first specs.

The 'no implementation prescriptions' assertion failed in all three baselines, each a different flavor: component paths + line numbers + diagnosis pointers (drag eval), cache/library mechanism speculation — React Query staleTime, SWR revalidateOnFocus (fuzzy eval), and a full implementation inventory with commit refs (CSV eval). This is the failure mode the skill was built to eliminate, and it eliminated it.

Non-discriminating assertions (passed in both configs): behavior-focused titles, observed-behavior problem sections, and eval 2's 'does not carry the bait' — baselines are already good at titles and, when research disproves a premise, at resisting it. These could be dropped or tightened in future iterations.

CSV eval premise was false: the scorecard CSV export already shipped (commit da5076b0, 2026-03-07) and BOTH runs independently discovered it. The contrast was still the sharpest of the three: with-skill respecced the issue as the real behavior gap (discoverability, with tests), baseline produced a 'confirm which gap applies / maybe close' triage document.

One genuine skill gap surfaced: the baseline drag run noticed weekday-named columns (Tuesday/Thursday) may only exist in the custom-columns prioritizer view, while the with-skill draft stated '/prioritizer/day-week' in its Problem section as fact. The skill's 'confirm current behavior' step did not force verification of the surface identification. Possible iteration-2 improvement.

Timing/tokens: no consistent skill overhead (with-skill 237s/548s/678s, 67.6k/71.1k/71.9k tokens vs baseline 572s/570s, 66.8k/55.6k). The fuzzy baseline (22.5s, 14.7k) is NOT comparable — it was a constrained no-research retry after two background-agent stalls.

Caveats: 1 run per configuration (small N, treat deltas directionally); grading was done inline by the orchestrating session (which also authored the skill) after the independent grader agent stalled — evidence quotes are in each grading.json for spot-checking; 3 background-agent stalls total were infrastructure, unrelated to the skill.
